concepts.label: Transport as a Lifeline
concepts.cardText: Goods and services do not move from supply locales to demand locales on their own, and their movement necessitates transport. The pace of development of a country depends upon the production of goods and services as well as their movement over space, so efficient means of transport are prerequisites for fast development. Movement can be over land, water and air, so transport is classified into land, water and air transport. Transport has been able to make the world a large village with the help of an equally developed communication system, so transport, communication and trade are complementary to each other.
concepts.hint: Why is efficient transport a prerequisite for development, and how are transport, communication and trade related?
concepts.probe: Why are transport and communication called the lifelines of a nation and its economy?

causeLinks.criterion: Connects the need to move goods and services from supply to demand locations to efficient transport being a prerequisite for fast development.

keyPoints.text: The movement of these goods and services from their supply locations to demand locations necessitates the need for transport. Thus, the pace of development of a country depends upon the production of goods and services as well as their movement over space. Therefore, efficient means of transport are prerequisites for fast development.

concepts.label: Importance of Roadways
concepts.cardText: India has the second largest road network in the world, about 62.16 lakh km (2020-21). Roadways preceded railways and still have an edge because of the ease with which they can be built and maintained. Road transport is growing in importance because construction cost of roads is much lower than railway lines, roads can traverse dissected and undulating topography and higher gradients such as the Himalayas, road transport is economical for few persons and smaller loads over short distances, it provides door-to-door service so loading and unloading costs are lower, and it is a feeder to other modes such as railway stations, air and sea ports.

concepts.label: Classes of Roads in India
concepts.cardText: In India, roads are classified into six classes according to their capacity. Golden Quadrilateral Super Highways link Delhi-Kolkata-Chennai-Mumbai and Delhi by six-lane highways, with the North-South corridor linking Srinagar and Kanniyakumari and the East-West corridor connecting Silchar and Porbander, implemented by the National Highway Authority of India (NHAI), to reduce the time and distance between mega cities. National Highways link extreme parts of the country and are the primary road systems. State Highways link a state capital with district headquarters. District Roads connect district headquarters with other places of the district. Other roads are rural roads linking villages with towns, which got impetus under the Pradhan Mantri Grameen Sadak Yojana so that every village is linked to a major town by an all season motorable road. Border roads are built by the Border Roads Organisation.

concepts.label: Border Roads and the Atal Tunnel
concepts.cardText: The Border Roads Organisation, a Government of India undertaking, constructs and maintains roads in the bordering areas of the country. It was established in 1960 for the development of roads of strategic importance in the northern and north-eastern border areas. These roads have improved accessibility in areas of difficult terrain and helped in their economic development. The Atal Tunnel (9.02 km), the world's longest highway tunnel, was built by the Border Roads Organisation in the Pir Panjal range. It connects Manali to the Lahul-Spiti valley throughout the year, whereas earlier the valley was cut off for about six months each year owing to heavy snowfall.

concepts.label: Metalled and Unmetalled Roads
concepts.cardText: Roads can also be classified on the basis of the type of material used for their construction, such as metalled and unmetalled roads. Metalled roads may be made of cement, concrete or even bitumen of coal, and therefore they are all weather roads. Unmetalled roads go out of use in the rainy season.

concepts.label: Role of Indian Railways
concepts.cardText: Railways are the principal mode of transportation for freight and passengers in India. They make it possible for people to conduct business, sightseeing and pilgrimage along with transporting goods over longer distances. Indian Railways have been a great integrating force for more than 150 years, binding the economic life of the country and accelerating the development of industry and agriculture. Indian Railways is the largest public sector undertaking in the country. The first train steamed off from Mumbai to Thane in 1853, covering 34 km, and the network is now reorganised into 17 zones. Today railways have become more important in the national economy than all other means of transport put together.

concepts.label: Distribution Pattern of the Railway Network
concepts.cardText: The distribution pattern of the railway network has been largely influenced by physiographic, economic and administrative factors. The northern plains, with vast level land, high population density and rich agricultural resources, provided the most favourable condition for growth, though the many rivers needing bridges posed some obstacles. In the hilly terrains of the peninsular region, tracks are laid through low hills, gaps or tunnels. The Himalayan regions are unfavourable because of high relief, sparse population and lack of economic opportunities. It was also difficult to lay lines on the sandy plain of western Rajasthan, the swamps of Gujarat and the forested tracts of Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Jharkhand. The Konkan railway along the west coast has facilitated movement of passengers and goods in recent times.

concepts.label: Railway Gauges and Problems of Rail Transport
concepts.cardText: The Indian Railway network runs on multiple gauge operations extending over 67,956 km, with broad gauge (1.676 m), metre gauge (1.000 m) and narrow gauge (0.762 and 0.610 m). Rail transport suffers from certain problems: many passengers travel without tickets, thefts and damaging of railway property have not stopped completely, and people stop trains and pull the chain unnecessarily, which causes heavy damage to the railway.

concepts.label: Pipelines
concepts.cardText: Pipeline transport is a new arrival on the transportation map of India. In the past pipelines carried water to cities and industries; now they transport crude oil, petroleum products and natural gas from oil and gas fields to refineries, fertilizer factories and big thermal power plants. Solids can be transported when converted into slurry. The far inland locations of refineries like Barauni, Mathura and Panipat could be thought of only because of pipelines. The initial cost of laying pipelines is high but subsequent running costs are minimal, and pipelines rule out trans-shipment losses or delays. There are three important networks: upper Assam to Kanpur, Salaya in Gujarat to Jalandhar in Punjab, and the Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur (HVJ) gas pipeline.

concepts.cardText: Since the ancient period India was one of the seafaring countries, and its seamen carried and spread Indian commerce and culture. Waterways are the cheapest means of transport and are most suitable for carrying heavy and bulky goods. They are a fuel-efficient and environment friendly mode of transport. India has inland navigation waterways of 14,500 km. 111 inland waterways, including 5 declared earlier, were declared National Waterways by the National Waterways Act, 2016. National Waterway No. 1 is the Ganga between Prayagraj and Haldia (1620 km), No. 2 the Brahmaputra between Sadiya and Dhubri (891 km), and No. 3 the West-Coast Canal in Kerala (205 km).

concepts.cardText: Deendayal Port (Kandla) in Kuchchh was the first port developed soon after Independence to ease the volume of trade on the Mumbai port, after the loss of Karachi port to Pakistan at Partition. It is a tidal port serving a productive granary and industrial belt. Mumbai is the biggest port, with a spacious natural and well-sheltered harbour. The Jawaharlal Nehru port was planned to decongest Mumbai and serve as a hub port. Mormugao port (Goa) is the premier iron ore exporting port and accounts for about fifty per cent of India's iron ore export. New Mangalore port in Karnataka caters to the export of iron ore concentrates from the Kudremukh mines. Cochin is the extreme south-western port, at the entrance of a lagoon with a natural harbour.

concepts.label: Communication: Postal Network

concepts.label: International Trade
concepts.cardText: The exchange of goods among people, states and countries is referred to as trade, and the market is the place where such exchanges take place. Trade between two countries is called international trade; it may take place through sea, air or land routes. Local trade is carried in cities, towns and villages and state level trade between two or more states. Advancement of international trade is an index of a country's economic prosperity, so it is considered the economic barometer for a country. As resources are space bound, no country can survive without international trade. The balance of trade is the difference between export and import: a favourable balance when exports exceed imports, an unfavourable balance when imports exceed exports. India exports gems and jewellery, chemicals and agricultural products, imports petroleum crude and products among others, and earns large foreign exchange through export of information technology.

checks.criterion: States that tourism promotes national integration, supports local handicrafts and cultural pursuits, and develops international understanding of our culture and heritage.

keyPoints.text: Foreign tourists visit India for heritage tourism, eco tourism, adventure tourism, cultural tourism, medical tourism and business tourism. There is a vast potential for development of tourism in all parts of the country.

checks.criterion: Names types of tourism foreign tourists come for, such as heritage, eco, adventure, cultural, medical or business tourism.
